_README: Client slug -> Google Places id. The sidecar that lets identity resolution
match a swept business against an existing client by place id rather than by
a slug derived from their name.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A FIELD ON SiteConfig:
packages/template/src/types/** is on CLAUDE.md's green-lane exclusion list and
outside this stream's grant. Promoting these ids into SiteConfig is a later
decision, not this stream's to make.
HOW IDS GET FILLED IN:
During the live acceptance sweep. The real clients are Bergen machine shops
and welders, so they appear in the sweep's own results — their ids are read
from there at NO extra Places call, which is why this stream can hold to
'zero calls beyond the sweep'. A displayName that does not match the client's
business name is left empty rather than guessed: a wrong place id silently
attaches one business's identity to another, and an empty one merely falls
back to the loud slug warning.
FILLED 2026-08-16 from data/prospects-scored.csv (the 2026-08-16 re-sweep),
zero Places calls. The bar was BOTH name and phone corroborating the client's
own config — name alone is not enough: a substring match on a row named
'Machines' with no phone hit two different client slugs and was rejected by
exactly that rule.
ks-welding-forge / -precision / -heritage spread `...ksWelding` and are the
same shop rendered in three design families, not three businesses. They carry
the same place id on purpose: the id identifies the business, and identity
resolution takes the first match, so the duplicate is harmless and makes the
client exclusion hold whichever slug is read first.
WHY THIS MATTERED: while every value here was "", client exclusion by place id
was inert, and the sweep offered KTS Machine Shop — an existing client — as a
prospect at rank 46 of the 2026-08-16 batch. See PR for ops/prospect-batch-50.
zz-fixture-phone-optional is a TEST FIXTURE, not a business. It has no place
id and never will.
